text:
Maria: quick sync — need a compact set of competitive rebut lines for the launch post + webinar CTAs. focus: infrastructure cost, predictable latency, and ops + fallbacks. short bullets we can hand to SDRs?
Ajay: can we prioritize 3 angles: predictable econ, production reliability, and deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private). one-liners + a 2-sentence backup each.
Tess: +1. also want 2 email subject lines for inbound routing tests (high intent vs research). A/B testable.
Sam: I'll toss in the tech hook about KV caching + batching — it's a strong econ story vs raw cloud endpoints.
Ben: sales wants a sharp objection handler for "we can just use cloud managed endpoints" — something like: "Cloud endpoints look easy until you hit 10k qps or strict data controls." short and punchy.
Maria: exactly. draft idea: 
- Headline: "Serving-first inference: predictable cost, not surprise bills"
- Rebut: "Managed endpoints hide per-token variability — Redwood lets you pin capacity and unit economics."
Ajay: alternate phrasing for marketing: 
- Headline alt: "Ship LLM features with production latency you can count on"
- Rebut alt: "Our routing, cache, and quantization profiles cut per-token cost without retraining."
Tess: email subjects: 
A: "Demo: Stable latency + predictable inference costs"
B: "How teams cut LLM serving costs 3x without model changes"
Sam: suggested short tech snippet for battlecard (1 line): 
"We combine KV prefix caching + workload-aware batching to reduce emitted tokens and server-side overhead — typical 2–4x unit-econ improvement vs on-demand endpoints."
Ben: objection handler for procurement: 
Q: "Why not just rent GPUs from cloud?"
A: "Reserved capacity + autoscaling policies mean committed cost maps to throughput — fewer surprise spend spikes and built-in fallback to compatible variants when capacity is constrained."
Maria: love that. can we get a quick matrix: competitor claim / our counter / proof point? keep 3 rows (cloud managed, LLM APIs, infra vendors). short.
Ajay: here — super short: 
- Cloud managed: "One API, varies in latency & price" -> Redwood: "Pin capacity & SLA-backed latency" -> Proof: "Dedicated pools + SLA; real customers show median p95 drop from 480ms -> 120ms."
- LLM APIs: "Access to many models, opaque perf" -> Redwood: "Model catalog + verified perf profiles" -> Proof: "Benchmarks across sequence lengths, quant profiles attached to each variant."
- Infra vendors: "You get infra but must build ops" -> Redwood: "Unified control plane + rollouts" -> Proof: "Canary + automatic fallback policies out-of-box; <2 person-week setup vs months."
Tess: can you compress that into 1-line soundbites for slides?
Sam: slide soundbites: 
- "Pin capacity, avoid surprise bills."
- "Verified perf profiles for every model we serve."
- "Turnkey ops for rollouts and fallbacks."
Maria: for webinar hook: open with a short customer story: "How X fintech cut inference spend 3x while improving p95 latency" then 20-min deep dive on routing & caching, 10-min panel Q&A.
Ben: put a CTA for Dedicated eval leads: "Get a 2-week dedicated capacity trial + cost forecast" — route those leads to sales-dedicated queue.
Tess: routing rules we should test: 
- webinar signups with company_size > 500 -> sales-dedicated
- product evals with "compliance" keyword -> enterprise-ops
- all others -> marketing-nurture
Maria: send me final bullets by EOD, I'll fold into the launch post draft and the battlecard. OpsBot: can you create a tracker for these A/B tests?
OpsBot: created tracker ticket: https://rwd-internal/track/PRJ-6297 (automated) :white_check_mark:
Maria: awesome, thank you. quick follow: Sam, can you attach benchmark artifacts (p95 charts + token-econ numbers) to the tracker?
Sam: will drop artifacts in the tracker by noon tomorrow.
Ben: I'll draft the SDR snippet deck with 3 quick rebut lines and email copy, share in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
Maria: perfect — let's reconvene tomorrow 10am to lock the final copy. cheers everyone :rocket:
